"AVX and AVX2 implemented, along with BMI1, BMI2, ADX, FMA, F16C and RDANDR extension!

0 : Disable AVX extension
1 : enable AVX, BMI1, F16C and VAES extension.
2 : All 1 plus enable AVX2, BMI2, FMA, ADX,VPCLMULQDQ and RDRAND.
"

Generate aligned atomics only (only available on Arm64 for now).

0 : Generate unaligned atomics handling code.
1 : Generate aligned atomics only, which is faster and smaller code size, but will cause SIGBUS for LOCK prefixed opcodes operating on aligned data addresses.

"Dynarec building BigBlock

0 : Don't try to build block as big as possible
1 : Build Dynarec block as big as possible
2 : Build Dynarec block bigger (continue when block overlaps, but only for blocks in elf memory)
3 : Build Dynarec block bigger (continue when block overlaps, for all types of memory)"

Ativar or disable the use of deferred flags.

0 : Desativar the use of deferred flags.
1 : Ativar the use of deferred flags.

Allow continue running a block that is unprotected and potentially dirty.

0 : Do not allow continue running a block that is unprotected and potentially dirty.
1 : Allow continue to run a dynablock that write data in the same page as code. It can gets faster in loading time of some game but can also get unexpected crashes.
2 : Will also, when it detect an HotPage, flag that page as NEVERCLEAN, and so it will not be write protected but Block build from that page will always be tested. It can be faster that way (but some SMC case might not be trapped).
Defines the max allowed forward value when building Block

Ativar or disable the use of native flags.

0 : Do not use native flags.
1 : Usar native flags when possible.

Ativar x86 PAUSE emulation, may help the performance of spinlocks.

0 : Ignorar x86 PAUSE instruction.
1 : Usar YIELD to emulate x86 PAUSE instruction.
2 : Usar WFI to emulate x86 PAUSE instruction.
3 : Usar SEVL+WFE to emulate x86 PAUSE instruction.

Handling of flags on CALL/RET opcodes

0 : Treats CALL/RET as if it never needed flags (faster, unstable)
1 : Most RET will need flags, most CALLS will not
2 : All CALL/RET will need flags (slower)

"Simulation of Strong Memória model

0 : Don't try anything special
1 : Ativar some Memória Barrier when writing to memory (on some MOV opcode)
2 : All 1 plus a Memória Barrier on every write to memory using MOV
3 : All 2 plus Memória Barrier when reading from memory and on some SSE/SSE2 opcodes"
Defines whether or not Dynarec will wait for the FillBlock to be ready

Tweak memory barriers to reduce performance impact of strong memory emulation

0 : Usar regular safe barriers
1 : Usar weak barriers for mild performance boost
2 : Usar weak barriers, additionally disable last write barriers

Controles tearing behaviour. Auto keeps DXVK defaults. True prefers mailbox-style presentation to hide tearing when VSincronizar is off. False allows a more relaxed mode that can reduce stutter when FPS drops, but tearing may appear.
Limits how many frames can queue ahead on DXGI and D3D9. Baixoer values can reduce input lag and improve pacing, but setting it too low may hurt performance in some games.
Enables DXVK tiler-oriented heuristics. This can help mobile Vulkan drivers such as Adreno/Turnip, but results depend on the game and driver version. Auto is the safest choice.
Creates the Vulkan surface on the first Present call instead of at swapchain creation time. Useful for some games that start with a black screen or initialize another renderer before DXVK.
Forces D3D11 textures to use a sample count of 1. This can improve performance or fix broken anti-aliasing in some games, but image quality may be lower.
Caps the maximum D3D11 tessellation level. Baixoer values can reduce GPU load and improve frame stability in games that overuse tessellation.
Substituirs presentation sync interval for DXGI and D3D9. -1 keeps the game default, 0 disables VSincronizar, and positive values force VSincronizar with repeated presents.
Limits the highest D3D11 feature level DXVK reports. Baixoering it can improve compatibility with games that fail on newer feature levels.
Forces a specific refresh rate for DXGI and D3D9 modes. Useful for games that pick the wrong Hz value, but use with care because some titles tie logic or physics to refresh rate.
Changes the shader model reported to old D3D9 games. Baixoer values can improve compatibility in legacy titles that misbehave with Shader Modol 3.
Controles floating-point quirk emulation in D3D9. Auto is safest, Strict is slowest but can fix broken old games, while True uses a faster approximation.
Substituirs anisotropic filtering level for D3D11 and D3D9 samplers. Can improve texture clarity, but may hurt performance or break effects in some games.
Controles DXVK memory defragmentation. Auto keeps the default behaviour, while forcing True may help long sessions and games that stream many assets, but can increase overhead on some devices.
Allows DXVK to use lower precision sine and cosine math where possible. This can slightly improve performance in shader-heavy games, but may introduce visual inaccuracies in rare cases.
Clamps negative texture LOD bias for D3D11 and D3D9. Can reduce texture shimmer and flicker, especially during camera movement, but may make the image look a bit softer.
Substituirs texture LOD bias for D3D11 and D3D9. Negative values sharpen textures but may increase shimmer, while positive values soften the image and can improve stability.
Sets how many threads DXVK may use for shader and pipeline compilation. Baixoer values can reduce CPU spikes on weaker devices, while higher values may reduce compile stutter on stronger CPUs.
Controles DXVK Gráficos Pipeline Biblioteca usage. It can reduce shader compilation stutter and speed up pipeline creation, but some driver versions behave better with it disabled.
Allows DXVK to use more relaxed D3D11 barrier handling. This may improve performance in some games, but it is experimental and can cause visual glitches or broken rendering.
